review.title: These work.  Use for coffee bean storage too. Of course you need the pump!
review.text:
Chardonnay, Sauv. blanc, Riesling, Pinot gris, Pinot blanc, Gewürztraminer, Pinot noir, Zinfandel, Gamay, Grenache, Sangiovese will benefit.

You can sparge the bottle with argon (expensive) or with nitrogen (remember nitogen and oxygen mix freely so use 3X the volume to ensure oxygen removal and seal quickly with a stopper.) The Vacu Vin is PRACTICAL and really cheap - less then a good bottle of wine. My stoppers are over a decade old. Remember to keep clean the stoppers and pump.

I use these for partial STILL wines in 375 ml and 750 ml bottles. Partial 187 ml bottles? Really - drink up. Yes, they work with screw cap bottles. Note: Some white wines have dissolved CO2 added during bottling - you will pull CO2 out of the wine INTO the headspace - that is really good beacause the oxygen will be sparged out of the bottle. I gently shake after pulling a vacuum to test if the wine has dissolved CO2 and vacuum again if needed - you do not want the stopper to come loose. The pump needs to click.

Try with a delicate white wine: Quarter fill bottle and seal with Vacu Vin and a quarter fill screw cap (yes, use a clean screw cap bottle because you probably put a hole in your cork or damaged the outside surface whereas the screw cap seals out oxygen.) Taste several days later: I always used my Vacu Vin stopper - lower oxidation and VA development.

For the purist: You have vacuumed off some volatiles. I pour from 750 ml to 375 ml screw cap bottle until slightly overflowing and seal then drink the remaining wine.which takes self-control and planning.

Heck, just buy bag-in-the-box wines! Forget all of this!

Suggestion for coffee beans:
1) I use the Vacu Vin to pulled the air out of the foil coffee bags and seal the vent with tape for storage until used later. I buy coffee beans when on sale and freeze for later. The bags if sound should have the vacuum.
2) After opening the package, I put my coffee beans into clean 375 ml bottles and use the Vacuvin to reduce the oxygen.

review.title: Good battery at value price...with one drawback.
review.text: I bought these batteries for a Canon 5D Mark III.  The Wasabi batteries are very well made and appear to last as long as or maybe even longer than the OEM Canon battery.  The only down side I have found is the camera does not "see" the battery, so it cannot display the battery status.  I was under the impression that these batteries had compatible computer chips in them to be able to interface with the camera's firmware and display their charge status.  Would have given them five stars if this feature was there.  Still, getting two quality batteries, a charger and a 3-year warranty is far better than spending twice this price for a single Canon battery.  Being able to charge your batteries via a cigarette lighter plug is also a very nice feature when you are out in the boondocks and do not have access to a 120v outlet.

review.title: Like putting a brand new heart in a dying laptop!!!
review.text:
I installed this new SSD into my wife's Toshiba laptop. As is with many PC's, it had become clogged with the multitude of Windows updates and miscellaneous "stuff." The boot time had gotten up to a few ticks short of three minutes. You could hear the original installed 7200 RPM HDD working, and working, and working...just to get everything opened. She was about ready to throw it out the window! This kit was very complete, and extremely easy to do. Just watch the couple How To videos on Kingston's website. Yes, it is as quick and easy to do as their videos show. I was done in under 25 minutes, and the vast majority of that was spent waiting for the cloning software to create the new drive. I do recommend going through your existing HDD and cleaning up the junk files prior to cloning it tot he new drive. No sense on starting out with a bunch of crap on your fresh new drive. The cloning software on the supplied CD was super easy to use and did a great job with just a few clicks of your mouse.

When I booted it up for the first time the time required for the system to completely boot up was right around 20 seconds!!! Subsequent boot ups were closer to 15 seconds. SMOKING fast. When the computer was up and running you could not tell anything on it had changed at all, except the super fast boot time. The desktop looked exactly like it did with the old drive. All shortcuts were exactly where they were and all worked. I have read a few reviews on this drive that said it was not a fast drive. While I have no actual testing data to back up my claims, I am telling you this drive is light years faster than the old HDD it replaced. Programs that used to take up to 15-20 seconds to load open up almost instantly. Click, and it is opened. No waiting. Is it the fastest SSD out there? Nope. Is it a darn good drive for the money? Absolutely!

So far I can't be happier with my decision to by this drive and swap out the old dinosaur HDD. It was like taking the shock paddles from the hospital and jump-starting new life into an old system. If you are on the fence about buying this drive, do not hesitate to pick it up. You won't be disappointed. Wifey is very happy too! As the saying goes...If momma ain't happy, ain't NO ONE gonna be happy!

review.title: Perfect Replacement for Shark 5 Series
review.text:
I bought this for our Shark NV581QR vacuum. It is a direct replacement for the Shark 500 series units. Shark WILL NOT sell you this part. They want you to buy their $100+ entire replacement head. To try to make sure you buy their parts only, Shark used security screw to hold the unit closed. YOU WILL NEED TO BUY A T-20 SECURITY TIP SCREWDRIVER TO REPLACE THE BEATER BAR ON YOUR OWN. I found a set of eleven sizes on Amazon for around $10. So bank on adding that cost into your purchase. Still WAY cheaper than the whole replacement head. Once it is installed the new beater bar will give your Shark all new life. Works like new again!

Installation is pretty basic once you have the T20 bit. To remove the old one you will need to gently pry out the square plastic pieces on each end of beater bar shaft. Slide the shaft out towards the belt side. Lift out the old part. You will need to put the new one in the belt and drop it into place first. Then slide the shaft through beater bar. Push the new plastic squares onto the ends and you're done. Reassemble the vacuum.

description: Utilizing a custom-formulated stone-derived coating from Germany, the Stone Frying Pan by Ozeri reigns with its ability to deliver non-stick perfection while remaining absolutely free of toxic substances such as APEO, GenX fluorinated chemicals, PFBS, PFOS, PFOA, and the lesser known NMP and NEP. According to the FDA, many of these chemicals constitute a worrisome class of nonstick compounds that have found their way into the food chain, including grocery store meats and seafood. Both the EPA and FDA have conducted toxicology research on exposure to some of these compounds that suggest associations with several kinds of cancers and health issues. Although the harmful PFOA and PFOS acids are being phased out of production, non-stick coatings today are often made with the aid of a new generation of fluoropolymers, known as GenX fluorinated chemicals and PFBS, which the EPA has more recently cited as suggestive of cancer and when consumed, may affect the kidneys, blood, immune system, liver and developing fetuses. Also of concern are APEO chemicals, which are restricted in Germany due to environmental concerns and toxicity in the food chain. By not using any of these ‘forever chemicals,’ the Stone Pan's coating stands ahead of the curve, achieving the highest marks for food safety and environmental health. In addition, the Stone Pan’s coating is applied using a water-based technique that is also free of the lesser known but potentially harmful chemicals NMP and NEP, sometimes found in cookware. The Stone Pan is far more durable and scratch-resistant than other non-stick surfaces, and always a breeze to clean. The Stone Frying Pan is made of a heavy-gauge aluminum core that allows for fast and even cooking without hot spots. It boasts a magnetized bottom for rapid heat transfer on induction stoves, and a heat-resistant silicone-coated handle. Coating made by Weilburger GmbH, Germany. Pan assembled in China.

What is RFID?

- RFID: Radio-frequency identification, uses electromagnetic fields to automatically identify and track tags attached to objects. The tags contain electronically stored information. Our Credit/Bank/ID card, passport have encoded chips tags, and stored our personal/private information. So, we should protect them from information hacker and data thieves.  - Data thieves can read your private data of cards at a distance of 10ft(3m), using a RFID scanner. Now, this RFID signal blocking wallet can protect your personal/private information safety.  - This item has built-in RFID signal blocking material layers, which can block signal from 10MHz to 30GHz. Credit/Debit/ID card, driver license, passport use the frequency of 13.56MHz. It won't block signal from ID badge, some old hotel room cards or building access cards, which use a frequency of 125 kHz.

description: La Tourangelle Toasted Sesame oil is pure, all-natural and handcrafted from high-quality sesame seeds harvested from South America or Africa. The seeds are toasted and then expeller (machine) pressed to extract the oil. This oil is filtered several times and then bottled. Our mill slowly roasts the sesame seeds using lower temperatures. The result is a deep amber, richly flavored oil with a subtle toasted taste. Sesame Oil has long been the universal cooking medium in Asia, imparting the characteristic flavor to the foods of its regions. In Chinese and Korean cuisine, it is added as a flavor highlight to cooked dishes. The Japanese often add about 10% toasted Sesame Oil to the oil used for tempura or deep-frying, creating a rich, background flavor. American cooks may want to use Sesame Oil to flavor an Asian stir-fry or noodle dish or as a marinade for meat or fish. Sesame Oil, rice vinegar, fresh grated ginger, and mustard is a delicious dressing for any combination of salad greens. Sesame Oil, is an ancient ingredient. The Assyrians used it as a cooking oil more than 600 years before Christ. It was expensive, however, and a hundred years later in Persia only the rich could afford it. It is still used as a medicine in India , and oil pressed from the raw seed is a massage oil in Ayurvedic medicine. Its low saturated fatty acid content and high unsaturated fatty acid content makes it a very healthy oil. La Tourangelle is one of few remaining oil mills keeping a time-honored French heritage of roasting and pressing nut kernels into delicious oils. We are a family-owned company whose mastery of oil production is the fruit of passion, integrity, and pride. We strive to be the best artisan oil producer, dedicated to making carefully crafted, sustainable, natural products. With artisan care, we extract the seeds' essence and hidden natural treasures to create amazing products that bring delight in the kitchen and well being for the body.

review.title: Bads Docs, Bad Support, But Works as It Should
review.text:
First the bad news. The manual is incorrect in its explanation of the LED indicators. An LED is on only if the associated port is active. An LED never flashes.

Also, the manual is incorrect in its explanation of entering hot key mode. The minus ("-") key should be held for considerably LESS than one second.

Finally, telephone customer support is impossible even well after the holidays. I waited 30 minutes and gave up.

But, once I figured out that the manual is wrong, I set up the device and it functioned as it should. Moreover, it works flawlessly with my Logitech wireless keyboard and mouse. I did have to use another USB keyboard to set up the device because my wireless keyboard lacks a scroll lock key. No biggie. Once the unit had been set up, I was easily sble to assign the CTRL key as an alternate hotkey.

So, the documents and support get a "D" but the design and implementation get an "A."

review.title: Good Value Despite Some Shortcomings
review.text:
Purchased on sale at Sams Club. Included microphone fails to drive unit to acceptable output volume. Substituting another microphone did not resolve the issue. Added a Nady MM-14FX Mini Line Mixer and got acceptable output levels similar to those produced by the built-in AM/FM tuner.

Note that this updated unit has only one mic level control rather than one for each channel. It also lacks the Line Out feature that enabled linking multiple units.

For convenience, I also added an Audio Technica ATR288W VHF Battery-Powered TwinMic Microphone System, which works well in my application even though it's an inexpensive ($120) VHF unit, since I don't require much range between the transmitter and receiver.

This unit has small wheels and I've seen owners drive their units at breakneck speed over bumpy sidewalks and even curbs, causing who knows what sort of stress/damage. No electronic device is designed to withstand such abuse. Possibly some of the complaints about reliability stem from this practice. I suggest giving the unit a break by getting a separate cart with wheels 3-4 inches in diameter.

All in all, good value. In retrospect, I might have preferred spending a few more dollars ($220) for the Samson XP40IW, which seems to have more power and to work well without the addition of third-party accessories. That unit is also available with a wireless mic ($298), though only a handheld not a lavalier/headset as required by my application.

But being able to put bread in the toaster without having to bend or fold it--the result of doing so is unevenly toasted bread--is right near the top of my list of desirable toaster characteristics. review.title: Status light lit but no heat
review.text:
The unit was received in good order but, once set up, the status light is lit but the unit doesn't heat. Customer service rep "Jacob" at Cuisinart advises no troubleshooting is possible and recommends return to Amazon. However, my own experimentation prior to my call demonstrated that a poorly inserted grill plate could fail to disable the safety interlock and that the status light is lit even when the interlock is enabled. So a poorly inserted plate COULD explain the observed problem. Of course, I had satisfied myself that this was NOT the problem in my case before placing the call.

Cuisinart manufacturing rates one star for poor quality assurance. This, of course, could be a statistical fluke. I may be the unlucky customer in 10,000 for all I know. But, with high confidence, Cuisinart customer support rates one star for a don't-bother-us approach to troubleshooting and for failure to offer the reasonably required apology for the ruined meal that would have been cooked on the grill.

In retrospect, I find that Google discloses a fair number of reviews citing the same, or a similar, malfunction. One has to wonder whether the apparent quality problem extends only to initial use or to product life. I'm not sure I want to find out.

review.title: Cloned fine but system not bootable
review.text:
Based on my experience I believe that I could reasonably rate this product at one star but I'm not absolutely certain exactly where to attribute fault. So I have given the benefit of doubt by rating the product at four stars.

The product cloned my existing 100-GB Windows 7 drive perfectly, in less than 15 minutes. The system then booted once but failed to boot after that, with error 0xc0000e, which indicates a problem in the boot setup. To my surprise and frustration a one-day-old system repair disk would not repair the boot information, insisting that it was not appropriate for the installed version of Windows. I was eventually able to persuade the repair disk to work by temporarily modifying the BIOS settings to hide all non-system drives. After that all is good.

The bottom line is that I found the entire experience of using this product significantly stressful. My working hypothesis is that the Windows 7 boot process references hard disk partitions by GUID rather than partition number and so my cloned disk was not bootable without adjustment of the boot information. I'm not sure that hypothesis adequately explains why I was able to boot the system once. I haven't bothered to study the issue further since everything is now working.

Lessons learned: (1) I strongly urge that a fresh system repair disk be made before initiating the clone process. (2) I suggest that the clone process be undertaken only by those with strong troubleshooting skills and with a working Internet-capable system apart from the system being modified, to support Internet search for troubleshooting information and assistance.

review.title: Stainless Steel, You Say? Nope! Shame on You, Farberware!
review.text:
I decided to toughen my original review, which appears beginning in the second paragraph, below. And I lowered the score from 3 starts to 1 star. The reason? As made clear in the original review, the "stainless steel" scoop is ONLY PARTIALLY stainless steel. This began to bug me more and more after the scoop failed. Granted, the product description nowhere says that the scoop is entirely stainless steel. But it gives that impression. And ads that give the impression of one thing when reality is something else are more than annoying. They rightly cast deep doubt on the integrity of the company that uses such "artful" language. Shame on you, Farberware. But you'll not fool me ever again because never again will I knowingly purchase a Farberware product. For me, its that big a deal.

For 5-10 years this was a fairly good scoop. The only failing was a tendency for the metal surface to pit and so look unattractive and even unsanitary. But that was mere appearance and easily disregarded. However, the other day the handle split in two. What had seemed to be a metal handle was revealed to be some sort of plastic or nylon that eventually gave way, outdone by a carton of ice cream. And so it goes for one more Farberware product. At one time I associated that name with quality and durability. But after the failures of "lifetime" pot handles and now this scoop, I'm not sure what has changed. Is it that the quality of the brand has, like so many, declined? Or was I wrong all along, as made clear by access to better information? I don't know. All I do know is that I'm now suspicious of alleged "Farberware quality."

review.title: No suds
review.text:
I’ve ordered this product several times and I’m generally quite satisfied. But one recent order contained soapless sponges. I don’t mean that the suds were sparse. On the contrary they were entirely absent. I see several other reviews that seem to describe the same experience. Apparently the production line occasionally runs out of soap and sometimes not all the defective units are found and culled.

This by itself would not earn a one-star review. Even the best production process can be expected to yield a small number of defects. Here, the complicating factor is that the product is sold as-is: that is, returns and refunds are not allowed. One might suppose that cases such as this, in which the product is plainly defective, might be an exception. However, I learned that no returns and no refunds means exactly that. And, to my surprise in the context of Amazon’s excellent customer service, I discovered there was no recourse beyond the seller. I was forced to eat the cost of the unusable order. Therefore, I have assigned a rating of only one star. Buyer beware.

review.title: Great for the price

This Nakiri/cleaver (it could be considered either) is great for the price, a real bargain. It’s quite sharp, as indicated by a paper test (see Google). The handle is comfortable and the knife appears to be well made. The knife has the full tang that’s necessary to durability.

review.title: Not So Sharp
review.text:
I purchased the VegitPro knife because of several reviews attesting to its sharp edge. Using a paper test of sharpness (see Google), I compared the VegitPro knife to several other ceramic knives of roughly similar cost (with one exception), made by Farberware, Kyocera, and Shenzhen. I also compared it to a metal knife made by FindKing.

To my surprise, I found that the VegitPro was the least sharp ceramic knife. Judging by its performance I would actually consider it dull. Moreover, all the ceramic knives fared poorly in comparison to the metal knife (FindKing), which was also less costly than the VegitPro and therefore a significantly better value.

Given my results, how does one explain the many reviews citing unusually high sharpness? I see two possibilities. Either the reviewers are mistaken or, for some reason, the VegitPro knife that I received is significantly less sharp than the typical VegitPro knife. Neither alternative seems subjectively likely and I can think of no immediate way to choose between them. Because the VegitPro knife that I received was dull, I made arrangements to return it. Once my purchase price has been refunded, I plan to obtain and test another VegitPro knife. This should go a long way toward settling the issue of the VegitPro’s sharpness.

Given that reviews critiquing the sharpness of the VegitPro knife are relatively few, I would neither be surprised nor offended if readers of this review are skeptical of my conclusions. Fortunately, they can easily settle the question themselves by performing their own test. Google for information on the so-called paper test of knife sharpness and see YouTube for examples. I would be very interested in seeing the results of such testing posted here.

Those buyers of metal knives who care about sharpness can acquire and use their own sharpener. However, I’m confident that relatively few home users possess the means to sharpen a ceramic knife. Manufacturers of metal knives may ship their knives with less than optimal edges for fear of accidents leading to costly lawsuits but manufacturers of ceramic knives lack this option. So, the factory sharpness of a ceramic knife would seem to be of vital importance.

This waterproof hiking shoe keeps your feet dry and lets them breathe, and the aggressive outsole bites into varied terrains. It's built for all-day comfort and offers a contoured heel lock. KEEN makes shoes to make a difference. From the products it makes, to the actions the it takes, KEEN inspires people to live and work monumental every day. Targhee II Hiking Shoe

Available in shoe and boot styles, Keen Men's Targhee II is the ideal hiking partner. The rugged Targhee II gives you the comfort and support of an athletic shoe and the resilience and protective features of a rough-and-tough hiking boot. Rugged Style with a Waterproof Nubuck Upper

The Targhee II offers a sleek-and-sporty style and a lace-up front for a custom fit. This low-profile shoe stands up to any trail conditions and looks good doing it, thanks to a durable, waterproof nubuck upper with stitching accents and pops of bright color on the laces and around the heel.
Breathable Moisture Protection with Keen.Dry

To keep you treading comfortably on all kinds of terrain, the Targhee II features a Keen.Dry insert. This waterproof membrane offers an additional barrier against moisture yet is breathable enough for all-day comfort.
S3 Heel Support

S3 stands for Shock, Suspension, and Stability and refers to Keen's unique heel-support structure. S3 is engineered to support the foot on impact, which dissipates shock, helping to prevent injury to the ankle.
Keen Metatomical Footbed and EVA Midsole for Support

For comfort and support that won't quit, the Targhee II features a removable, dual-density EVA footbed that provides arch support by hugging the natural contours of your foot. The compression-molded EVA midsole extends the benefits of the footbed and adds an extra spring to your step.
ESS Shank Reduces Foot Fatigue

To keep you going longer, the Targhee II has a torsional-stability ESS shank in the midsole. This shank helps to stabilize your foot as you move, minimizing fatigue, so you can enjoy every moment as you push on to the next crest.
Multi-Directional Lugs for Greater Traction

To give you a steady grip on all kinds of terrain, the Targhee has 4-millimeter, multi-directional lugs on its non-marking rubber outsole. These lugs are spaced wide apart to "bite" into the terrain, giving you more dependable traction on slippery and uneven surfaces.
Patented Toe Protection

Because rocky objects and debris can trip you up on the trail, the Targhee II includes Keen.Protect, patented toe protection that wraps up and over the outsole for thorough coverage of the entire toe bed.
Keen: A Story of Hybrid Innovation

Keen began in 2003 with an inspired sandal design that combined comfort and toe protection. This radical design departure for sandals spawned the overriding Keen philosophy of hybrid innovation--striving to create new possibilities and to discover and implement original ideas.

Keen products put an emphasis on the joys of play. At the same time, Keen believes in the value of working hard to give back to the community. Timex Group B.V. is one of the best-known American watch companies. Timex's U.S. headquarters are located in Middlebury Connecticut and it has substantial operations in China, the Philippines and India and full scale sales companies in Canada, the UK, France and Mexico.

The company began in 1854 as Waterbury Clock in Connecticut's Naugatuck Valley, known during the nineteenth century as the "Switzerland of America." Sister company Waterbury Watch manufactured the first inexpensive mechanical pocket watch in 1880. During World War I, Waterbury began making wristwatches, which had only just become popular, and in 1933 it made history by creating the first Mickey Mouse clock under license from Walt Disney, with Mickey's hands pointing the time.

During World War II, Waterbury renamed itself U.S. Time Company. In 1950 the company introduced a wristwatch called the Timex. Over the next three decades, Timex was sold through a series of advertisements which emphasized its durability by putting the watch through "torture tests," such as falling over the Grand Coulee Dam or being strapped to the propeller of an outboard motor, with the slogan "It takes a licking and keeps on ticking." With the help of former Olympic broadcaster, spokesman John Cameron Swayze, sales took off. The company later became Timex Corporation, then Timex Group and, to date, has sold over one billion watches.

The company has remained very competitive and the Timex brand continues its dominance through present day. Its primary market remains the United States and Canada, although the Timex brand is sold worldwide due to its ability to capitalize on its strong brand image and reputation for quality.

One of the most successful and important features available on many Timex watches is the Indiglo backlight system. Indiglo is a brand name of Indiglo Corporation, solely owned by Timex for licensing purposes. Timex electroluminescent lamps, branded Indiglo, were introduced in 1992 in the Ironman watch line. They were an immediate success. The Indiglo lamp uniformly lights the surface of the Timex’s watch dials in a manner that makes the dial read very easily in many different light settings. In some newer watches the Indiglo backlight only lights up the numbers, rather than the entire LCD display, which is achieved by means of a specialized film that inverts the LCD transmissivity.

Today, Timex Group products are manufactured in the Far East and in Switzerland often based on technology that continues to be developed in the United States and in Germany. With a large and varied line of watches, Timex has the style for everyone. From the locker room to the board room, there is a great Timex style time-piece for you.

There are varying reasons for tooth sensitivity, and the two main systems - potassium nitrate and arginine - work completely differently to lessen or prevent tooth nerve pain.. Neither system will help everyone. I use both kinds of toothpaste - KNO3 in the evening and arginine in the morning - with the understanding that they somewhat counteract one another, but using both gives me relief against heat/cold, vibration, pressure, and age-exposed roots. Pro-Relief Mouthwash adds an extra layer of protection to my morning brushing.
This product has a measuring device WITHIN the cap so that you don't use more than necessary - fill the inner measuring device, not the whole cap. The viscosity is greater than usual mouthwashes and might take a little getting used to. The flavor is ok, not as flavorful as US products but more flavorful than some other European and especially Asian products. If you have tongue, gum, and cheek tissue sensitivity to peppermint-type flavorings, this will add a slight bit to that sensitivity. If you are accustomed to using a mouthwash after brushing, make this that mouthwash. Using Pro-Relief Mouthwash before brushing with a non-arginine toothpaste or using a "breath freshener" mouthwash after the Pro-Relief Mouthwash largely wastes your purchase.

review.title: The Rollator for Tall People
review.text:
The Carex Crosstour Rolling Walker Rollator will let this six-footer stand up straight while walking. The handles rise high enough for maybe up to 6'3" depending on arm length. The front wheels are big enough to get over normal driveway cracks, tar-sealed slabs, finger-sized roots, and street to drive transitions. At the end of the rear wheels is a foot pedal that you can step on to help raise one front wheel at a time to get over obstacles. As with other similar rollators, you have to be careful not to put your fingers around the seat tubes when pushing down to extend and lock the sides. The seat pulls up easily with a handle to collapse and fold, and the rollator is steady on its wheels while folded.
The stowage packet is good for books, writing pads, and smaller laptops and tablets, but I think it would be not so good for shopping, folded coats, large purses, or anything thicker that five inches. The packet is thinner, perhaps, to make folding more practical.
I have found this rollator to be sufficiently steady for walking our small dog with me on the road side of the curb and him exploring as far as his leash will reach. It's best to stay on the roadway rather than putting the inside wheels in the curbing, as this causes the rollator to pull toward the curb. The seat, even with its retractor handle, is comfortable enough for resting. The handles feel to me like they are put on backwards left-to-right, but it's much too difficult if not impossible to get them off to see if they would offer more hand and wrist support on the other side, and they are not a problem, just strangely shaped. The safety reflectors are inadequate, but it's nothing some reflective tape won't solve. The brakes work fine, I just don't use them very much. I can get this rollator up our front door steps by lifting the front end one or two steps at a time. It's light enough not to hurt my bad back and arthritic knees.

review.title: It may taste like grass, but there ARE ways around it!
review.text: This stuff is a great supplement for your diet, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking to improve their health.  First, lets address the taste...Honestly, the way they tell you to make it on the label isn't very good.  It indeed DOES taste like grass clippings.  To the people saying they like it...well I guess they like the taste of grass.  But I'm pretty sure it's safe to say most of us don't lol.  With that being said, there are tons of ways to make it taste better so don't let those review deter you!  You don't have to make it the way they say, and it's just a guideline.  I personally have been making green smoothies for breakfast with all fresh fruits and veggies for a bit now.  Then I saw this and noticed all of awesome nutrition packed into it that I had to give it a go.  What I did was just sub the "green" portion of my smoothies with this stuff and leaving the rest of my recipe the same.  I put 1/3 cup of the The Ultimate Meal, 2 red pears, 2 bananas, 4 tbs of chia seeds, and 2 cups of almond milk.  This really helps the taste, and makes it palatable.  It does still have the grassy taste, but the pears really sweeten it up and make it enjoyable.  I now look forward to the "green" flavor and crave it.  Just a warning though, you could do half the amount of chia seeds if you don't like texture but I personally don't mind it.  With my said recipe you're looking at a seriously healthy breakfast.  It will contain all the fiber you need, calcium, almost all your magnesium, and many more nutrients you need for the day.  Basically the powder contains loads of vitamins and minerals, but how you get them down is on you.  I'm sure the recipe was made the way it was to keep costs down for the consumer, but I don't mind spending a little extra on fresh fruit to make it taste good.

review.title: Well they aren't hyping up some garbage product that are going to disappoint you
review.text:
Everything you hoped for...finally here!

Yes, these are it! Have you been doing your research? Reading all the latest headphone reviews? Watching all the youtube reviews? Well they aren't hyping up some garbage product that are going to disappoint you. These are the headphones you've been waiting for!

Tired of those gimmicky "bass heavy" cans that rattle your ear drums but completely disregard any kind of high end clarity? Look no further my friends! These will give you that boomy, satisfying bass, but still emphasize all the detail you long for.

I've tried lot of headphones and I can say without a doubt these are the best you can get for 300 bucks. Beats, Sennheisers HD7s, Bose QC's, Audio Technica M50X, the list goes on...I just always seem to come back to these. They have that balance that seem to satisfy my ear drums most consistently. You get that low end punch, but all the trebley detail as well.

A lot of time you will get a headphone that has rich bass, but lacks the highs. Or a headphone that has a beautiful neutral sound, but will lack any of that exciting bass we all crave. These babies incorporate the best of both worlds...I have read some reviews saying these aren't bassy enough...that is the biggest load of b/s I've ever heard. These have PLENTY of bass. Anymore is just overkill and will compromise the overall sound. And yes...I am a basshead. So don't think I'm some little girlyman that can't handle the rumble of a good 808 kick drum! I love EDM and dubstep, and if a headphone can't make me feel the bass I disregard it. These absolutely, positively, do NOT leave you wanting more in the bass department. Just the perfect amount to back up those gorgeous mids!

Aside from the sound. The build quality is amazing. Very comfortable. Although I do wish they include the XL ear pads because the stock ones are a bit small, but still very comfy. I did order the XL ones though to have both. My Sennheiser HD7's came with two different sets of cushions which I did really appreciate. The way they fold is up great, and paired with the case they give you, traveling is no problem! Very sturdy, well built headphones!

Anyway...it's 2:20am, and i'm sitting here writing this review for YOU as I'm jamming some tunes on my m100's! I'm just so blown away by them that I felt the need to write this essay of a review in the middle of the night...for YOU! I know you're sitting in your chair wondering, "damn, should I buy these really expensive, beautiful headphones?" And the answer is ABSOLUTELY!

review.title: WOW!!  So much for so little!!
review.text:
All I can say is WOW!

I can't believe I have all of this power for this price...this stereo will leave your ears ringing for days if you have it in a small room, I kid you not. What sold me on this bad boy was not the 700watts of power, but the fact that it was perfect right out of the box. A small sub dedicated to your bass, and two huge speakers w/ tweeters to help sculpt a good overall sound. BIG sound. This isn't your average joe stereo. It sounds like a mini PA system lol!

That being said, I wouldn't say the speakers are anything to write home about either. They are very detailed in their delivery, but not the clearest speakers I've ever heard. LG really geared this unit at people who like a lot of low end, and it delivers that and some. That is not say these speakers don't have have any kind of clarity because they do thanks to the tweeters, but don't expect anything really ground breaking going on. Overall though, the sound is very listenable and doesn't ever leave you cringing from them being unbalanced or anything like that. I can say that I enjoy the sound actually. And this is coming from someone who has a lot of high quality audio products (Bose, Klipsch, KRK, Roland, V-Moda, Sennheiser, JBL, etc.) so I'm kinda hard to please lol.

There are two things though that I would say I'm not pleased about. The build is very, very cheap. I suppose this is how they get away with keeping the price down, but I wouldn't want this thing in my living room on display at all. This would be great in a garage, bedroom, dorm room, man cave, or something similar. Lots of plastic used, but the speaker boxes are particle board which is good for an enclosure. Everything else (and I mean everything) is plastic though. Secondly, there is no way of tuning it at all. You have a button to increase bass, but that is it. I'll say I do like the way they have it configured so thumbs up for that, but would be cool to have adjustment. Can't have it all though right?

Ultimately though I am very, very pleased with this purchase. After setting it up I sat back with my jaw on the floor astonished at how loud this thing gets...and it's under 200 dollars! It's a no brainier, and I assure you there is nothing that will come close to this for the money.

features: Pure butter shortbread cookies
description: Product Description

Walkers Shortbread is Scottish baking at its best! The shortbread is made with just four all natural ingredients: butter, flour, sugar, salt. Made in the Highlands of Scotland in the small village of Aberlour to their original Scottish family recipe which have made its cookies famous worldwide.
From the Manufacturer
BRAND STORY

The Walkers story begins over a hundred years ago in 1898 in the Scottish Highlands, when the twenty-one year old Joseph Walker opened the doors of his own bakery with a loan of £50 and the dream of making the finest shortbread in the world. In the first year of business, Joseph used every spare moment to perfect his shortbread recipe, and it was time well spent.

As his fame spread, and demand increased for his quality shortbread, Joseph took the first steps to expanding the business by moving to a larger shop in the Speyside village of Aberlour and investing in a horse and cart to deliver his baking further afield.

During the 30s, the business - like Joseph's family - was expanding. Two of his sons - James and Joseph - joined the business, bringing fresh, new ideas with them. By 1936, they had introduced three valuable additions to the business: a range of cakes, a selection of confectionery - and the company's first delivery van. Now Walkers produce could be sold even further afield, and the prospects for expansion were looking promising.

While some manufacturers began to cut corners by using margarine instead of butter, Joseph believed that people still appreciated the care that went into making a superior product like Walkers shortbread. And he was right. That's why, even after Joseph Walker died in 1954, his sons continued to use his original recipe.

Demand grew, and so did the business. By 1961, all three of James' children - Joseph, James and Marjorie - had joined the business, making the third generation of Walkers working for the family firm. By 1975, Walkers had outgrown their extended bakery, and moved to a custom built factory that gave them the extra space and facilities they needed to develop new products such as Chocolate Chip Shortbread and specialty cookies.

By the 1970s, Joseph's grandchildren had begun exporting Walkers shortbread to over 60 countries around the world - still baking to his original recipe. Within a decade, they won the first of three Queen's Awards for Export Achievement - the highest accolade given to British exporters.

Then, as now, Walkers stayed in touch with their customers by testing every new product in Aberlour's village shop. So, customers around the world are enjoying a range of products that were first given the seal of approval by the villagers of Aberlour. Consistent quality and traditionally delicious recipes have made Walkers the choice of the most discerning customers and retailers.

Walkers reputation grows day by day as loyal customers worldwide delight in traditional shortbreads and innovative new products like almond, ginger and luxurious chocolate covered shortbread. All Walkers' products are packaged in its unmistakable red tartan and proudly bearing the image of Bonnie Prince Charlie and Flora MacDonald, the image which captures one of the most romantic moments from Scotland’s history, and reflects all the tradition and care that goes into baking every piece of Walkers shortbread.
The quality and natural goodness of Walkers has attracted many international awards, including five gold Mondiale medals and the Food from Britain Innovation Award.

While Joseph's children and grandchildren have moved with the times, they have always remained true to his original ideal - and his original recipe. So, when the family opened a new factory at Elgin to produce their popular new range of shortbread cookies and biscuits, they naturally still insisted on using only the finest ingredients: plump fruits, aromatic spices, chunks of real chocolate and flavorsome nuts. And there's not an artificial flavoring, coloring or preservative in sight. Just as Joseph Walker guaranteed all those years ago.

Today, Joseph would be proud to know that his great grandchildren are carrying on the family tradition and are now the fourth generation of Walkers to make 'The world's classic pure butter shortbread'.

product_info.title: JBL GTO8608C 6-Inch x 8-Inch/5-Inch x 7-Inch 2-Way Component System
features: 6" x 8" / 5" x 7" two-way component system with woofer, tweeter, crossover and mounting system
Plus One woofer cone with rubber surround
One-inch mylar-titanium tweeter
Outboard crossover with tweeter-level control
210 Watts peak power handling; 2 ohm impedance
description: Product Description
JBL 6" x 8"/5" x 7" 2-Way Component System
Amazon.com

Take your car audio to the next level with this 6" x 8" / 5" x 7" two-way component system, featuring JBL's Plus One woofer cone, 1" My-Ti Edge-driven Dome Tweeter, and I-Mount mounting system and outboard Crossover system.
The GTO tweeter is both strong and light weight while being adjustable
The Plus One woofer cone increases  bass output and efficiency
Why JBL Sound?

For more than 60 years, JBL products have been bringing home the impact and excitement of the world's best recording studios, movie theaters and concert venues. Now, JBL engineers are creating these world-class listening experiences in the car. Thanks to advanced technology developed in the professional arena, JBL mobile products simply sound better than the competition. High output, superb bass response, long life and smooth response are all things you can expect from any speaker that wears the JBL badge. So join enthusiasts who know audio, and don't settle for anything but JBL in your vehicle. Bring the sound of the show on the road.
Listen Loud

The last thing you want to worry about is the quality of your speakers. We understand. All new JBL mobile products have to go through nearly 500 hours of environmental testing. We put them under temperatures fluctuating between -35°C and +90°C with up to 90 percent air humidity for more than 200 hours. We expose speakers to UV light for more than 150 hours to simulate a mounting location on a car's rear deck. We even shake things up, as all of our new mobile audio products have to pass extensive vibration testing before we release them for production. We've made unparalleled efforts to ensure the best possible quality so that you can listen long and loud when you crank up a JBL speaker.
Edge-Driven, Mylar-Titanium Tweeter

The JBL GTO8608C component system uses a 1-inch (25-millimeter) Mylar-titanium (My-Ti) tweeter with a large voice coil--much like a voice coil found in high-end home audio speakers. The benefit of the Mylar and titanium blend in making a tweeter is that it is lightweight and has remarkable strength. At the same time, its large voice coil increases power handling and reduces distortion at high output levels. This tweeter design also helps create more seamless integration with the woofer. The GTO8608C's tweeter is even adjustable, so you can modify it to optimize the sound. The result? True, high-end, audiophile-quality performance.
The in-line crossover network creates seamless sound with the woofer
Click to Enlarge
Look for the True 4 ohm logo for the best real world performance
Computer-Optimized Outboard Crossover

When you want the best sound possible in your vehicle, only a JBL system will do. Like a high-end JBL home speaker, the JBL GTO8608C component system employs a high-quality, computer-optimized outboard crossover that accurately and smoothly projects sound where it needs to go. Think of the crossover as a traffic cop for directing sound. When your music reaches your GTO8608C speaker system from your amplifier or head unit, the crossover directs high frequencies to the tweeter and the midrange, and low frequencies to the woofer. Since we have engineered the crossover specifically for the high performance of the GTO8608C component system, it provides incredible detail, smooth midrange and increased power handling. The GTO8608C delivers an extraordinary listening experience that you would never expect to hear in the front seat of a car.
Bass that Booms
Plus One Cone

The JBL GTO8608C component system uses a 5" X 7" woofer with the patent-pending JBL Plus One cone technology. Plus One technology gives the GTO8608C more cone surface than competing models of the same size--up to 30 percent more in many cases. With a larger cone area, the GTO8608C speakers provide higher efficiency and better bass response. Add a low-Q woofer design for higher bass output from the typical mounting location and 210-watt peak power handling, and the GTO8608C will really get your car booming.
The patented Starfish and I-Mount tweeter mount system optimizes sound quality and makes install into factory systems easy.
Click to Enlarge
Powerful Performance
True 4-Ohm Topology

Low-impedance speaker voice coils extract more power from your amp for more powerful performance than high-impedance coils do. JBL GTO8608C component-system speakers use a lower-impedance voice coil than a typical 4-ohm speaker to extract the most power possible from all amplifiers engineered to drive loads of 4 ohms or less. And the GTO8608C component system is compatible with both aftermarket head units and factory-installed systems. Since many factory-installed systems incorporate 2-ohm speakers and include amplifiers designed to drive 2-ohm loads, replacing those reduced-impedance speakers with a typical 4-ohm model will reduce the power output from the amplifier. For the most powerful performance, the GTO8608C component system makes the best use of any amplifier by providing an optimum 2-ohm load.
An Easy Install
I-Mount Tweeter-Mounting System

If you are upgrading the sound in your vehicle to the GTO8608C component system, JBL's proprietary I-Mount (patent no. 5,859,917) tweeter system makes it easy to flush-mount or surface-mount the tweeter. But being easy to mount isn't enough. A tweeter has to sound good as well. If you flush-mount the GTO8608C, you can use our innovative flush-mount cup to angle the tweeters and lock them into the best angle for optimum response and imaging.
Starfish Tweeter-Mounting System

What about when you want to replace the factory-installed component system that comes in many of today's vehicles while keeping that �factory-built" look? JBL engineering has made that easy, too. The GTO8608C features JBL's Starfish tweeter-mounting system. It simplifies mounting the tweeter in any number of ways behind factory grilles and panels, and it doesn't require any special modifications.
And with such easy installation, you'll be listening to your new JBL speakers in no time at all.
The JBL GTO8608c component system delivers high output, superb bass response, long life and smooth response.

review.title: Completely unacceptable for windowed environments
review.text:
I bought this monitor to upgrade my 8-year old 19-incher from HP (model f1903), which I've always been happy with, so I assumed this HP product would be good as well. Unfortunately, no. Where the old one handled the conditions of my windowed office admirably, this one is completely unsuited for that purpose. I suppose the literally mirror-like glossy finish on the screen might make for good color in a dim environment, but it is completely unreadable when there is any significant light reflecting off it. Even without windows, but just average overhead interior lighting, you still see your own reflection quite brightly in the darker areas of the image. And don't even think about using it in a room with windows.

The worst part of this is that one of my reasons for choosing this monitor was that HP's description on Amazon advertises "Brightview technology to help reduce glare", which I assumed meant it would be at least somewhat average in the area of glare resistance. That is quite possibly the most underhanded, deceptive marketing description I've ever seen. Thanks a lot, HP!! If you had any decency you would have at least mentioned that it was a glossy screen which is designed for dim rooms only.

Needless to say, I'm returning the monitor primarily because of this glare issue, which is far and away worse than anything else I've ever owned, including several CRTs, which were famous for the problem. But in the interest of completeness, I'll move on to an overall summary of my impressions.

POSITIVE FEATURES:

1) I was pleasantly surprised by how slim and lightweight it was. Very nice looking.

NEGATIVE FEATURES:

1) Terrible glare (see above). Its glossy screen might be your thing if you're all about playing games in your basement man-cave, but is completely unacceptable for a windowed office environment.

2) Color-shift seemed much worse than average to me. At a 2-3 foot viewing distance the same shade of gray appears noticeably more pink towards the top of the monitor and blue toward the bottom. On further research I understand that some color-shift is to be expected on all of the cheaper, TN-type panels, but on most I've seen it hasn't been as noticeable as on this one.

3) Flimsy stand. I understand that this is a common problem as well, but this monitor seems worse than average to me. The problem is exacerbated by the placement and stiffness of the control buttons, which are impossible to operate without setting the monitor to wobbling.

review.title: Deeply Flawed Design
review.text:
I like the quality feel of this case, so I hate to give it a bad rating, but I have to point out its deeply flawed design. The problem is that the material in the front that goes around the edge of the tablet to hold it in place when the cover is opened covers too much of touch-screen, extending right to the very edge of the visible portion of the screen. It doesn't interfere with viewing, but it makes it difficult to swipe down the notification slide, and almost impossible to move an icon off the screen (i.e., from one home screen to another). You will find yourself having to take the tablet out of the case to do this.

You should also be warned that this case is more than an inch thick, with most of that thickness being in the back where your tablet doesn't even need much protection anyway. Just another mark of very poor design, in my opinion.

RC-R6 Universal Remote: Affordable Control of Your Home Theater

With your new home theater, you're ready to enjoy the best Hollywood has to offer. But you don't enjoy having a pile of remotes on your coffee table. Fortunately, Universal Remote Control has a way to make your home theater easy and fun to use.
Replace all your old remotes with the URC-R6 Universal Remote

The line of consumer remotes from Universal Remote Control allows you control your TV, Blu-ray, sound system and cable box with a simple, easy-to-use remote--one solution for your home theater. And it's more affordable than you may expect.

Sophisticated, custom residential URC solutions are available for the most extreme home theater installations. But if you just need an easy way to replace a stack of remotes with a simple but powerful solution, look no further. The URC-R6 simplifies your home entertainment experience like no other entry-level remote.
URC Consumer remote controls: helping you control the experience, one component at a time.
Replace Up to Six Remotes with One URC-R6

Perfect for DIY, the URC-R6 replaces up to six individual remote controls in an affordable, user-friendly design. URC's R6 remote works with thousands of A/V devices and has multiple set-up options, including device auto-search and a "Learning" feature.
Simplify Controlling Your Home Theater with MacroPower and Favorite Channels

In addition to being a great replacement for up to six remote controls, the URC-R6 delivers much more. MacroPower is a very useful way to make a lot of things happen with one button push. For example, in most home theaters, to watch television, the user must turn on the TV, then turn on the Cable Box or the Satellite Receiver, then turn on the Surround Sound system for sound. Instead of pressing all of those buttons one at a time, MacroPower enables you to turn on all of these components, in the sequence you want, with one button push.
Program up to five channels per button on the URC-R6's "My Favorites" buttons

The R6 uses one-button "Macros" that allow you turn on your TV, cable box, DVD player and surround sound system all at the same time with the press of one button. The URC-R6 also comes equipped with four customizable "My Favorites" buttons. You can program up to five favorite channels per button.
"Couch Mode"

The R6 remote is designed to automatically turn itself off if a button is pressed for more than 30 seconds. This prevents battery power from being depleted should the remote accidentally slip between the couch cushions.
SimpleSound Total System Volume

SimpleSound is one of the most exciting features of the R6. It gives you total volume control over ALL the components in your system, even those that do not have built--in volume control, such as TIVO, DVD and VCR. SimpleSound saves you the hassle and inconvenience of constantly switching between component modes just to control volume. So no matter what, there are no hassles when you quickly need to reduce or mute sound for a phone call or doorbell.
Channel Control "Punch Through"

This "Punch Through" enables you to program the R6 so that either the Cable or TV Channel Controls (CHANNEL UP, DOWN, LAST, CHANNEL NUMBERS 0-9, +10 and ENTER) will also operate in other component modes on the remote control.
Transport Control "Punch Through"

This "Punch Through" enables you to program the URC-R6 so that DVD or DVR Transport Controls (PLAY, STOP, FF, REW, PAUSE, SKIP and RECORD) will also operate in other component modes on the remote control.
OSD (On-Screen Display) Control "Punch Through"

This "Punch Through" enables you to program the URC-R6 so that CBL or DVD OSD Controls (MENU, GUIDE, INFO, EXIT, SEL and 4 Cursor Controls) will also operate in other component modes on the remote control.
The URC-R6 can learn from other remotes, allowing it to grow with your home theater
Learning Mode

This feature will allow you to literally teach the URC-R6 commands from other remote controls; when the remote is in learning mode, you can line the two remotes facing each other and transfer commands with just a few buttons presses. Press any button on the R6 remote that you want to teach a command to. For example, if you want to teach the MUTE button on the R6 remote the TV Mute command from the other remote, first press the MUTE button on the R6 remote and the TV component button LED light will blink once indicating that the R6 remote is ready to learn the command. This way, your remote is never obsolete--the URC-R6 grows with your home theater.

review.title: Nice, but limited
review.text:
This is my favorite remote control because I just like the feel and layout of it better than anything else I've tried. It's much better in my opinion than the newer URC models. The most commonly used buttons are all just where I want them to be, arranged to be accessed very easily without any awkward stretching of your thumb. However, it does have some some pretty severe shortcomings:

1) The pre-programmed codes are pretty limited. None of them worked for my Phillips DVR/DVD combo. This wouldn't be so bad except for limitation #2 (see below).

2) It's memory for learning remote control codes is VERY limited. It had just enough to learn all the most important buttons for my DVD/DVR, with only about 5 left over for my TV and audio receiver. Since I found pre-programmed codes for my TV and audio receiver that worked for most things, this turned out OK for me, but just barely. If you have more than one device that you have to program by learning all the buttons manually, this remote will not work for you.

3) The procedure for learning/programming is very awkward. No big deal since you only have to do this once, but other remotes have much more intuitive commands for programming.

4) It's layout is dated, with a +10 on the number pad instead of a dot as needed for DTV channels. This isn't a big deal since you can just reprogram the +10 to be a dot, but it would be nice if the label itself had a dot.

5) The IR beam is aimed straight out of the end of this remote instead of angled a little downwards. This means you have to contort your hand to point the thing straight at your TV system or it won't work. I actually took the thing apart and manually bent the little IR LED downward to fix this. Had to cut away some of the plastic housing to make room for this, which is a little ugly, but it works.

review.title: Quirky, and poor quality
review.text:
As is typical of Sony products in my experience, the interface for this remote is clunky, counter-intuitive, and poorly documented, making custom programming an extremely time-consuming process. Also, as others have noted, it seems to require fresh batteries and slow, deliberate button-presses for the programming to work at all, but even then it sometimes gets into a state where the command sequences just don't take. Worse, it inexplicably failed to program one button from my Onkyo receiver remote even when the others worked fine, no matter how often I retried and double-checked my process. I have a URC learning remote that has no problem with that button, so I can't imagine why the Sony does. If you can live with the pre-programmed setups for your devices it might be a decent remote for you, but in that case why bother buying a learning remote instead of just an ordinary universal remote? Bottom line, I've wasted enough time trying to get this piece of junk to work; I should have known better than to buy a Sony.

Update: Well, after my initial frustration subsided a bit, I stuck with it, and eventually ended up getting all my functions programmed, though some of them inexplicably took 3 or 4 tries. The secret is to do the programming in a dimly lit room; the process isn't completely reliable even then, but much more reliable than when the lights are on. There are still some strange and undocumented quirks, e.g., the behavior of a macro programmed with a single-press of an arrow key can sometimes activate multiple arrow presses. But now that I've worked around that (though I spent way too many hours doing so), the remote seems to be working pretty well. And I do like the way it fits in my hand.

Update #2: And now after about 8 months of normal use, some of the buttons have just stopped functioning. Very frustrating after having spent so many hours getting this thing customized. Either I'm unlucky and got a poorer-than-average quality unit, or Sony products are just cheap garbage, I guess. I'm reducing my rating to 2 stars.

review.title: Worse than garbage: probably damaged my camera
review.text:
I used this happily about 15 or 20 times, and then my expensive Panasonic G9 camera stopped connecting to any of my old 4/3 lenses through this adapter. On closer inspection, I noticed a deep groove had been worn right through the apparently-very-low-quality electrical contact pads of the adapter, and into the plastic beneath them. Worse yet, I could see that this wear had left tiny shavings in the body of my camera all around the contact pins, which not only explains why I had been getting what I assumed was dust on the sensor, but probably also why one of the pins wasn't moving very freely any more and therefore sometimes failing to connect even to my new micro-4/3 lenses without the adapter. (Of course, I can't absolutely PROVE that this problem was caused by the wearing of the adapter, but it seems VERY likely.)

Needless to say, I knew this was just a cheap imitation when bought it, but the official Olympus equivalent is so ridiculously overpriced that I figured it was worth a shot. Boy, was I wrong. Take my advice: DON'T DO IT!!!

review.title: Great concept, though with some room for improvement
review.text:
I've tried many different universal all-in-one remote controls over the years, and this is my new favorite! Its compact shape fits my hand nicely, its buttons feel clicky instead of mushy, and most of all, the scroll wheel to select devices is a pretty cool concept that works well for my needs. It's also much easier than most (other than the quirky and overpriced Logitech Harmony series) to program, and there are virtually no limitations to which functions or macros you can assign to which buttons. So it's basically a compulsive customizer's dream.

As much as I like it, I still can't give it a full 5 stars, however, due to so many areas where I feel it has some room for improvement. These aren't huge issues, but if you're thinking of buying it, you might want to be aware of them. Specifically, here's my list:

1) It doesn't have as many buttons as most other models. Which means you will have to leave off many extended functions that your TV and other devices have special buttons for (such as closed captioning, view modes, smart features, DVD options, previous and next, etc.).

[BTW, my workaround for this problem is to set up duplicate devices that function like a Shift or Fn key on the number pad. For example, I have a "TV#" device in addition to my regular "TV" device, with some extended functions programmed to the number buttons for this device. So I can scroll forward to the "TV#" device to access these extended functions, or scroll back to the "TV" device to use the number pad normally. (The difficulty is in remembering which numbers are assigned to which functions, of course, especially since there's not really enough room to attach many labels.)]

2) Related to issue #1 above, I wish the scroll wheel was clickable like a button in addition to being scrollable. It would be so nice to be able to scroll to the device you want to operate and then just click to select the TV input mode that corresponds to it, for example.

3) Speaking of the buttons, they are unfortunately not backlit, which is pretty common, but I also find them a bit difficult to distinguish by feel. It would be nice if some of the common ones (like mute) had a different texture or raised bump or something, to let you know your finger is on the right place even in the dark.

4) Final complaint about the buttons: The ones for the number pad are very small, which makes them kind of hard to use.

5) The app for programming the remote control is not real well designed in my opinion, even though it is certainly a LOT nicer than having to enter special programming codes on the remote control itself, like most other models require. The biggest problem I have with it is that it doesn't seem to save your configuration in the app (in contrast to Logitech's Harmony system, for example), but instead just loads it back up from your remote control every time you connect. So if your remote control ever breaks and you have to replace it, I guess you'll have to start over from scratch instead of just restoring your saved configuration to your replacement.

6) Another issue with the programming app is its database of devices. Although I had no problem finding all the devices I wanted to use, the list of functions for several of these devices was confusingly labelled and missing some important functions, and the default button mapping for the device seemed poorly thought out. So I had to spend a lot more time than I should have reassigning buttons and learning new functions that should have been included. (Fortunately, the app makes it very easy to learn whatever new functions you need from your original remote control.)

7) As others have noted, the IR beam from this remote control seems a little weaker and/or narrower than with many other models, requiring you to point it more directly at the device you want to control.

8) Finally, the remote control itself seems perhaps a little cheaply made to me. For example, the light from the display leaks a bit through the sides, which I suppose is an indication of fairly thin plastic construction. It's not terrible by any means, but I'm just a little worried that it might not stand up to heavy use for very long. Time will tell, I guess...

--

All in all, I really do highly recommend this remote control in spite of these minor shortcomings. I'm very happy with it.

review.title: Slide feature is nice, but width all the way down to the ends is annoying
review.text:
The really nice thing about this strap is that it's made of low-friction material like a seatbelt, so it glides or "slides" (as the name implies) easily across your shoulder. This allows you to carry your camera on your side or back of the hip with the strap across the opposite shoulder and then easily rotate it around and bring it up to your eye to shoot. It works surprisingly well. Other straps tend to grip and bind on your back and shoulder when you try to do this, but this one makes it easy.

The puck-style quick disconnects are also nice, but not really anything to write home about. I find the classic squeeze or pinch-style mini-disconnects found on many MUCH cheaper straps works just as well, and if anything probably take up slightly less space.

The main annoyance I have with this strap is the fact that its width goes all the way down to the ends where it gets in the way of using your camera. Other straps get narrow at the ends, which makes it much easier to pick up your camera without the strap getting in the way of your hands (or without it interfering as much even if it does get in the way). This also makes this strap bulkier than it needs to be, taking up more room when you stow your camera in a bag. As far as I'm concerned, if Peak Design would redesign their strap to fix this, they'd have a 5-star product on their hands.

review.title: Connectivity is a hassle
review.text:
The Achilles heel of this dash cam is the way you access videos (or the live feed) through your phone with the Drive app. It basically only works when you're parked in your garage, since it requires the camera to be in range of your home WiFi, and even then it's very slow and finicky, because the app has to shut down your phone's internet connection and establish a WiFi connection to the camera (for data transfer, not internet) instead every time you want to access anything (if I understand it correctly).

This connection process didn't work reliably at all for me until I updated the firmware (using my computer, since the phone app basically couldn't establish a connection) and went through a few other hassles to clear caches and reset things. I'm not even sure what eventually got it to start working, but it definitely wasn't plug-and-play. And it's still slow to connect, even after the reliability issues got sorted out (hopefully).

The saving grace is that once you get everything set up and working, you probably won't have to access the camera via your phone very often, so the slowness to connect may just be a minor annoyance and not an actual deal breaker.

Moka is the Italian Way to Make Espresso

Authentic espresso is the heritage of the Italian culture and tradition, and the great Italian tradition of coffee making began with moka. Found in most Italian kitchens for more than half a century, moka produces an inherently aromatic espresso. It is more intense in flavor, and more pure in coffee taste. That is why generations of Italians have sworn by stovetop moka espresso makers.

In fact, in Italy every family owns at least two mokas. Used on the stovetop, the heat from the burner boils the water and directs it up through the ground coffee and into the receptacle, producing a perfect espresso every time.

Why an Electric Moka Espresso Maker? Although the traditional stovetop moka makes great espresso, people have been searching for a safe, convenient and easy-to-use alternative. review.title: Coffee wasn't hot enough
review.text: Our biggest gripe about this product was the fact that we had to microwave the coffee once it was finished as it was not hot like a drip coffee maker. There's no handle or relief to lift it out (see pic). Essentially you have to turn the pot over and catch it with your hand. Not good when hot or when there's a little liquid left. You would have to pry the unit out with a knife or something to get it out while upright. We unfortunately will return this unit.

review.title: Just was I was Looking for
review.text:
I was in the market for an item like this around 4 months ago.
There wasn't anything worthwhile at the time.
Most Bluetooth speakers where designed around usage for hands free cell phones and did not support any Fidelity.
At the time I purchased some x-mini miniature wired speakers that were great for the money but still attached via wires.

I give kudos to Logitech in defining this market need and acting on it with a fairly priced, well built and functional product. The carrying pouch is a classy added touch.

The unit was paired to my iPad in a matter of 30 to 40 seconds and reconnects consistently so far.
The sound quality is what I expected and so far I am pleased.

I normally make most of my electronics purchases of this nature through Amazon but given that I had $25.00 in Best Buy rewards I purchased mine at the local store.

Go ahead. Take the plunge. Buy these and you won't be disappointed.

11/24/2010

Update: One problem that most people, including myself, had with these speakers was that there was no control of the volume from the ipad via bluetooth. This has now been resolved with the release of iOS4.2.1!

The Bissell SpotBot Pet might actually be a dog or cat owner's best friend. Puppy training "accidents," spit-up hairballs, the occasional half-eaten chicken carcass: with pets in the house, cleaning challenges come with the territory. Some of the worst mishaps happen when there's no one around, creating set-in stains that resist the most stubborn scrubbing with a sponge or rag. This pet-friendly compact deep cleaner does all its work hands free, meaning users can fold laundry, wash dishes, even walk the carcass-scatterer while the mess gets cleaned up. To use, clear away excess debris and place the cleaner over the spot. Timex Group B.V. is one of the best-known American watch companies. Timex's U.S. headquarters are located in Middlebury Connecticut and it has substantial operations in China, the Philippines and India and full scale sales companies in Canada, the UK, France and Mexico.

The company began in 1854 as Waterbury Clock in Connecticut's Naugatuck Valley, known during the nineteenth century as the "Switzerland of America." Sister company Waterbury Watch manufactured the first inexpensive mechanical pocket watch in 1880. During World War I, Waterbury began making wristwatches, which had only just become popular, and in 1933 it made history by creating the first Mickey Mouse clock under license from Walt Disney, with Mickey's hands pointing the time.

During World War II, Waterbury renamed itself U.S. Time Company. In 1950 the company introduced a wristwatch called the Timex. Over the next three decades, Timex was sold through a series of advertisements which emphasized its durability by putting the watch through "torture tests," such as falling over the Grand Coulee Dam or being strapped to the propeller of an outboard motor, with the slogan "It takes a licking and keeps on ticking." With the help of former Olympic broadcaster, spokesman John Cameron Swayze, sales took off. The company later became Timex Corporation, then Timex Group and, to date, has sold over one billion watches.

The company has remained very competitive and the Timex brand continues its dominance through present day. Its primary market remains the United States and Canada, although the Timex brand is sold worldwide due to its ability to capitalize on its strong brand image and reputation for quality.

One of the most successful and important features available on many Timex watches is the Indiglo backlight system. Indiglo is a brand name of Indiglo Corporation, solely owned by Timex for licensing purposes. Timex electroluminescent lamps, branded Indiglo, were introduced in 1992 in the Ironman watch line. They were an immediate success. The Indiglo lamp uniformly lights the surface of the Timex’s watch dials in a manner that makes the dial read very easily in many different light settings. In some newer watches the Indiglo backlight only lights up the numbers, rather than the entire LCD display, which is achieved by means of a specialized film that inverts the LCD transmissivity.

Today, Timex Group products are manufactured in the Far East and in Switzerland often based on technology that continues to be developed in the United States and in Germany. With a large and varied line of watches, Timex has the style for everyone. From the locker room to the board room, there is a great Timex style time-piece for you.

review.title: This is great cookie mix!

The company began in 1854 as Waterbury Clock in Connecticut's Naugatuck Valley, known during the nineteenth century as the "Switzerland of America." Sister company Waterbury Watch manufactured the first inexpensive mechanical pocket watch in 1880. During World War I, Waterbury began making wristwatches, which had only just become popular, and in 1933 it made history by creating the first Mickey Mouse clock under license from Walt Disney, with Mickey's hands pointing the time.

During World War II, Waterbury renamed itself U.S. Time Company. In 1950 the company introduced a wristwatch called the Timex. Over the next three decades, Timex was sold through a series of advertisements which emphasized its durability by putting the watch through "torture tests," such as falling over the Grand Coulee Dam or being strapped to the propeller of an outboard motor, with the slogan "It takes a licking and keeps on ticking." With the help of former Olympic broadcaster, spokesman John Cameron Swayze, sales took off. The company later became Timex Corporation, then Timex Group and, to date, has sold over one billion watches.

The company has remained very competitive and the Timex brand continues its dominance through present day. Its primary market remains the United States and Canada, although the Timex brand is sold worldwide due to its ability to capitalize on its strong brand image and reputation for quality.

One of the most successful and important features available on many Timex watches is the Indiglo backlight system. Indiglo is a brand name of Indiglo Corporation, solely owned by Timex for licensing purposes. Timex electroluminescent lamps, branded Indiglo, were introduced in 1992 in the Ironman watch line. They were an immediate success. The Indiglo lamp uniformly lights the surface of the Timex’s watch dials in a manner that makes the dial read very easily in many different light settings. In some newer watches the Indiglo backlight only lights up the numbers, rather than the entire LCD display, which is achieved by means of a specialized film that inverts the LCD transmissivity.

Today, Timex Group products are manufactured in the Far East and in Switzerland often based on technology that continues to be developed in the United States and in Germany. With a large and varied line of watches, Timex has the style for everyone. From the locker room to the board room, there is a great Timex style time-piece for you.

description: Lace low boot

Dr. Martens is the stuff of legends. It all began near Munich, Germany in 1945 when Dr. Klaus Maertens injured his foot in a skiing accident in the Bavarian Alps. To make walking easier during the healing process, he designed a shoe with an air-cushioned sole. Using old rubber tires, he constructed soles that had air trapped within closed compartments. He showed his prototype to his engineer/inventor friend, Dr. Herbert Funck, and together they decided to develop and produce the shoes. Not only did the shoe solve the doctor's immediate problem, but it also started to sell well in Germany. By 1959 the two decided that they needed a company to produce and distribute the shoes, then called Dr. Maertens, in other parts of the world. At first, many manufacturers rejected the concept of an air cushioned sole as a short-lived gimmick. However, the R. Griggs Group, located in the village of Wollaston in England, decided to go along with the idea by creating the first work boot with the revolutionary sole. On the first of April 1960, the first cherry red eight-eyelet work boot was produced and named 1460. To sell the brand name better in England, the name was anglicized to Dr. Martens. The range was branded AirWair and the rest is history.
